entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Pharasmanes I of Iberia was a key ruler of the third Pharnavazid dynasty, reigning from 1 to 58 CE and playing a prominent role in the eastern lands of the Roman Empire under Tiberius, Caligula, Claudius, and Nero. His reign transformed Iberia into the Transcaucasian empire, dominating the kingdoms of Armenia, Georgia, and Albania. Pharasmanes I was a member of the royal family and was known for his military campaigns and strategic alliances with neighboring kingdoms. He was also mentioned on the Stele of Vespasian, a significant archaeological find that provides valuable insights into the history of the region. The legacy of Pharasmanes I can be seen in the continued influence of the Transcaucasian empire on the modern-day politics and culture of the region. Despite the passage of time, his name remains synonymous with bravery and strategic brilliance in the annals of Iberian history.
